HARPREET SINGH BRAR J. (ORAL)

The present petition has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter 'Cr.P.C.') seeking quashing of complaint dated 05.09.2017 bearing no. COMI/203/2017 filed under Sections 420, 406, 120-B of the IPC titled as "Rubesh Monga v. Anupma Singla and others"(Annexure P-1) along with summoning order dated 08.01.2018(Annexure P-2), charge sheet dated 07.06.2023(Annexure P-3), amended charge sheet dated 01.09.2023(Annexure P-4) passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bathinda.

sentences.text: FACTUAL BACKGROUND 2.
The facts of the case, briefly, are that petitioner no. 2 allured the respondent to invest money with Ablaze Info Solution assuring him a handsome return.
In order to convince him, he showed the respondent the account statement of his wife-petitioner no. 1 and informed him that she is in- charge of the area for the company.

He further informed the respondent that he 1 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:025460 CRM-M-51028-2023 2 2024:PHHC:025460 and his wife have Anupma Singla And Anr vs Rubesh Monga on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128700700/
1 received Rs. 10 to 20 lakh after investing in the said company.

entities.text: Anupma Singla And Anr vs Rubesh Monga
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent was required to click on online advertisements of different companies for which he would be paid Rs. 20 to 25 per like.
Petitioner no. 2 further assured him a regular income of Rs. 2750 per day which would be transferred directly to his bank account.

Convinced by the same, the respondent invested Rs.
1,72,500/- in the aforesaid company.
However, the respondent did not receive any money from the petitioners or the company.
The respondent asked the petitioners to return the money invested by him with interest but they failed to do so.
The petitioners proclaimed that their intention was merely to cheat the respondent and will not refund any of his investment.

3. The respondent filed an application dated 25.04.2017 before SSP, Bathinda pursuant to which statements of the respondent-complainant and witnesses were recorded, however, no further action was taken.
On finding a prima facie case against the petitioners, the learned trial Court issued summoning order dated 08.01.2018 against them.
Thereafter, charges under Section 420 read with 120-B of IPC were framed against them vide order dated 01.09.2023.
CONTENTIONS 4.

Learned counsel for the petitioners contends that the amount was transferred directly to the account of M/s Ablaze Info Solutions Pvt. Ltd. and the same is corroborated by record of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (Annexure P-5).

Further, the WhatsApp chat annexed by the respondent with the complaint cannot be read into evidence in view of Section 12 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 and Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
2 of 6

Neutral Citation No:=2024:PH CRM-M-51028-2023 3 2024:PHHC:025460 5. He further submits that there was no intention to cheat since the inception on behalf of the petitioners, as such, the offence under Section 420 of the IPC is not made out.
The respondent and petitioner no. 2 are good friends, engaged in similar work of multilevel marketing and have no association with M/s Ablaze Info Solutions Pvt. Ltd.
An FIR has been registered against Abhinav Mittal, Managing Director of the said company but the learned trial Court did not find any incriminating material against the petitioners.
Finally, charges were framed against petitioner no. 2 vide order dated 07.06.2023(Annexure P-3) and the name of petitioner no. 1 does not find a mention in the same.

Thereafter, the charge sheet was amended vide order dated 01.09.2023(Annexure P-4) to include the name of petitioner no. 1 and remove the name of Abhinav Anupma Singla And Anr vs Rubesh Monga on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128700700/
2 Mittal as the accused.

sentences.text: The order dated 01.09.2023(Annexure P-4) was erroneously ratified by learned trial Court by ignoring Section 362 of the Cr.P.C.

As such the instant complaint deserves to be quashed in view of judgments rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Abhishek v. State of Madhya Pradesh 2023 AIR SC 4209 and Parveen @Sonu v. State of Haryana 2022 AIR SC 270 as well as the Rajasthan High Court in N.S. Kothari (Dr.) v. State of Rajasthan 2004(2) Cr.L.R. (Raj.)
948.
6.

sentences.text:
Per contra learned counsel for the respondent contends that the petitioners cheated the respondent and got him to transfer Rs. 1,72,500/- on 06.01.2017 to M/s Ablaze Info Solutions Pvt.
Ltd.
During investigation, it was discovered that commission was received directly in the account of the petitioners.
The respondent and his family have been fraudulently coaxed into investing a total of Rs. 8,62,000/- into the said company.
Hence, the trial Court has correctly appreciated the facts of the case to frame charges against the petitioners.

Reliance in this regard can be place of the judgment rendered by 3 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:025460 CRM-M-51028-2023 4 2024:PHHC:025460 the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Niranjan Singh Karam Singh Punjabi v.
Jitendra Bhimraj Bijja and ors. 1990 AIR SC 1962.
7.

Niranjan Singh Karam Singh Punjabi v.
Jitendra Bhimraj Bijja and ors. 1990 AIR SC 1962
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is further contended by the learned counsel for the respondent that the culpable intention to cheat from the very inception is discernible from the allegations enunciated in the complaint (supra)
filed by the respondent.

Moreover, the respondent-complainant has placed on record the whatsapp messenger chat between him and the concerned petitioner which leaves no doubt with regard to the complicity of the petitioners qua their intention to cheat the respondent from the very inception.
OBSERVATION AND ANALYSIS 8.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and after perusing the record of the case, this Court is of the opinion that whether or not the whatsapp messenger chat produced by the respondent-complainant is admissible would be a moot question to be determined by the learned trial Court on the basis of the evidence adduced by the respondent-complainant as interference by this Court with regards to factual questions is impermissible in law as it is the sole prerogative of the trial Court to determine the disputed questions of fact after examining the evidence on record.

Thus,
disputed questions of facts cannot be delved into at the pre-trial stage while dealing with a case of quashing of FIR or complaint under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
9.

A two Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in HMT Watches Ltd Vs. M.A. Abida (2015) 11 SCC 776 has held as under: -
"10......... Whether the cheques were given as security or not, or whether there was outstanding liability or not is a question of fact which could have been determined only by the trial court after recording evidence of the parties.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

In our opinion, the High Court should not have expressed its view on the disputed questions of fact in a petition under section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
to 4 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:025460 CRM-M-51028-2023 5 2024:PHHC:025460 come to a conclusion that the offence is not made out.

The High Court has erred in law in going into Anupma Singla And Anr vs Rubesh Monga on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128700700/
3 the factual aspects of the matter which were not admitted between the parties."

10. A two Judge bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the Rathish Babu Unnikrishnan Vs. State (Govt. of NCT) 2022 SCC Online SC 513, speaking through Justice Hrishikesh Roy, observed as under:
"17.

entities.text: Rathish Babu Unnikrishnan Vs. State (Govt. of NCT) 2022 SCC Online SC 513
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The consequences of scuttling the criminal process at a pre-trial stage can be grave and irreparable.

Quashing proceedings at preliminary stages will result in finality without the parties having had an opportunity to adduce evidence and the consequence then is that the proper forum i.e., the trial Court is ousted from weighing the material evidence.
If this is allowed, the accused may be given an un-merited advantage in the criminal process.

Also because of the legal presumption,
when the cheque and the signature are not disputed by the appellant, the balance of convenience at this stage is in favour of the complainant/prosecution, as the accused will have due opportunity to adduce defence evidence during the trial, to rebut the presumption."
11.

In Sampelly Satyanarayana Rao Vs. Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency Limited (2016) 10 SCC 458, a two Judge bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, speaking through Justice Adarsh Kumar Goel, made the following observations:

entities.text: Sampelly Satyanarayana Rao Vs. Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency Limited (2016) 10 SCC 458
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "17. As is clear from the above observations of this Court, it is well settled that while dealing with a quashing petition, the Court has ordinarily to proceed on the basis of averments in the complaint.
The defence of the accused cannot be considered at this stage.
The court considering the prayer for quashing does not adjudicate upon a disputed question of fact."
CONCLUSION 12.
In view of the discussion above, this Court cannot appreciate the probable defence set up by the petitioners at this stage.
Accordingly, the present petition is dismissed.
